stated_limitation: Sequential replay within individual ripple events, tested with a rank-order correlation and a rigorous per-event and population-level shuffle control, did not reach significance in this single 40-minute session with ~34 place cells. This is an honest negative result at the single-event level: published significant single-event replay detection typically uses substantially larger simultaneously-recorded ensembles (in the hundreds of cells) and/or pools across many more ripples/sessions than are available here.

justification.dataset: DANDI 000044 (Grosmark & Buzsaki dorsal CA1, PRE/MAZE/POST) is the canonical dataset for sharp-wave ripples and replay.
justification.handling: Data streamed from S3 with correct int16-to-volts conversion, NREM/state filtering, excitatory-unit selection, and a well-justified re-linearization validated against the sparse official one.
justification.analysis: Standard ripple detection, place fields, Bayesian decoding, and a shuffle-controlled rank-order replay test with both per-event and population nulls, complemented by EV/REV reactivation with its accepted reverse control.
justification.correctness: Every reported number (488 ripples, 34 place cells, 3.2% significant, global p=0.92, EV=0.029 vs REV=0.001) is internally consistent, reproduces from the committed code, and is physically possible.
justification.figures: Ripple, place-field, significance, and reactivation panels are clear and labeled, but fig3 selects the four highest-|wcorr| events as illustrative examples against a null result, which is flattering though disclosed.
justification.honesty: The write-up reports the negative single-event replay result plainly, explains the underpowering, hedges the weak reactivation as merely directional, and names specific limitations.
justification.verdict: Robust ripple detection, an honestly reported null replay result, and a cautiously stated reactivation effect make this work I would accept from a rotation student.
